turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen's essay got a zero and nobody called me.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Found where? Before you walk me through anything, who decided on the zero?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
11:31. Created isn't the same as written, and a file can be made at any hour. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
A paste means he had text somewhere else first. Kids draft in a notes app and paste it in. Show me the history itself, not your summary of it.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
I'm not here for your respect. The history, Hale. Show me the page with those times on it.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
A line misremembered from a play is a student's mistake, not proof of anything else. Which three editions, and where in the essay does it appear? Put the page in front of me.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
I have a job. Which three editions, Hale, and where is that line in the essay?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
A student changing his argument between an outline and an essay is called revising. Teachers usually encourage it. Put the October 15 outline next to the essay where I can read both.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to rely on it alone. Your own procedure says the same. Take the score off the table and give me the strongest thing you have, on paper.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
I'm not here to do your job, Hale, and there is no off the record. You called this meeting, so answer me: who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.
A rewrite for what? Everything you've told me is your say-so, and none of it is in front of me. And you still haven't said whether the zero comes off.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? That's an odd thing to ask a parent. Does the zero come off, Hale, yes or no?
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Take it to the vice principal. I'm going to the principal today, and then the board. I'll want everything you've told me in writing first.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither. The zero comes off, and then you show me what you've got.
